subject: HEALTH
title: Health 6
description: Grade 6 health education aligned to the 2008 California Health Education Content Standards, which focus sixth grade on Mental, Emotional and Social Health; Injury Prevention and Safety; and Personal and Community Health. Students learn to identify emotions, manage stress, build self-esteem, communicate assertively, resolve conflict, prevent bullying and stay safe online, and recognize when to seek mental-health help. They then practice injury prevention, first aid, 911 calls and California earthquake/wildfire preparedness, study disease prevention, immunity and consumer health, and finish with a community health advocacy project.
framework: 2008 California Health Education Content Standards (Grade 6: Mental, Emotional and Social Health; Injury Prevention and Safety; Personal and Community Health); 2019 CA Health Education Framework

standards.H-6.1.1.M: Identify a wide range of emotions and describe healthy ways to express them.
standards.H-6.1.2.M: Describe the causes and effects of stress and identify positive coping strategies.
standards.H-6.1.3.M: Describe characteristics of healthy and unhealthy friendships and relationships.
standards.H-6.1.4.M: Describe bullying, cyberbullying, harassment and their effects on individuals and communities.
standards.H-6.1.5.M: Explain the importance of respecting individual differences, including culture, ability, gender and family structure.
standards.H-6.1.6.M: Recognize signs of depression, anxiety and other mental health concerns and when to seek help.
standards.H-6.1.7.M: Explain how self-esteem, resilience and a growth mindset contribute to mental health.
standards.H-6.2.1.M: Analyze how family, peers, social media and culture influence emotions, self-image and behavior.
standards.H-6.3.1.M: Identify trusted adults, school and community resources for mental health support, including crisis lines.
standards.H-6.4.1.M: Use effective communication skills (I-messages, active listening) and conflict-resolution strategies.
standards.H-6.5.1.M: Use a decision-making process to address social situations and peer pressure.
standards.H-6.6.1.M: Set and monitor a goal to improve mental, emotional or social health.
standards.H-6.8.1.M: Advocate for respect, kindness and bullying prevention.
standards.H-6.1.1.S: Identify ways to prevent injuries at home, in water, in sports and in the community.
standards.H-6.1.2.S: Describe basic first aid procedures for common injuries and emergencies.
standards.H-6.1.3.S: Describe emergency and disaster preparedness procedures, including earthquakes, fires and wildfires.
standards.H-6.1.4.S: Describe safe and responsible use of the internet, social media and digital devices.
standards.H-6.1.5.S: Identify ways to prevent violence and recognize the dangers of weapons and gangs.
standards.H-6.1.6.S: Describe pedestrian, bicycle, skateboard and passenger safety practices.
standards.H-6.2.1.S: Analyze how peers, media and the desire for thrills influence risk-taking behavior.
standards.H-6.3.1.S: Identify emergency resources and how to access them, including calling 911.
standards.H-6.4.1.S: Demonstrate communication and refusal skills to avoid or escape unsafe situations.
standards.H-6.5.1.S: Use a decision-making process to evaluate safety risks.
standards.H-6.7.1.S: Practice injury-prevention, first aid and emergency-preparedness skills.
standards.H-6.8.1.S: Encourage others to follow safety practices.
standards.H-6.1.1.P: Describe personal hygiene and dental health practices for adolescents.
standards.H-6.1.2.P: Explain the importance of adequate sleep and healthy screen-time habits.
standards.H-6.1.3.P: Distinguish between communicable and noncommunicable diseases and describe how the immune system works.
standards.H-6.1.4.P: Describe ways to prevent the spread of communicable diseases, including handwashing and immunizations.
standards.H-6.1.5.P: Describe sun safety and the protection of eyes and hearing.
standards.H-6.1.6.P: Describe how environmental factors (air, water, noise) affect personal and community health.
standards.H-6.2.1.P: Analyze how advertising influences the purchase of health products and services.
standards.H-6.3.1.P: Access valid health information, products and services, and identify health-care providers.
standards.H-6.5.1.P: Use a decision-making process to choose health products and services.
standards.H-6.6.1.P: Set a goal to improve a personal health practice.
standards.H-6.7.1.P: Practice behaviors that reduce the risk of disease and protect personal health.
standards.H-6.8.1.P: Advocate for a healthy home, school and community environment.

units.title: Wellness and Health Skills
units.big_idea: Health has physical, mental/emotional and social sides that we strengthen with skills.

units.title: Emotions, Stress and Self-Esteem
units.big_idea: Understanding emotions and managing stress builds resilience.

units.title: Healthy Relationships and Communication
units.big_idea: Respectful communication keeps friendships and families strong.

units.title: Respect, Bullying Prevention and Digital Citizenship
units.big_idea: Everyone deserves respect online and offline, and bystanders can make a difference.

units.title: Mental Health and Getting Help
units.big_idea: Mental health concerns are common and treatable; asking for help is a strength.

units.title: Injury Prevention and First Aid
units.big_idea: Most injuries are preventable, and first aid skills can save lives.

units.title: Emergency and Disaster Preparedness
units.big_idea: Preparing before an emergency keeps families safe in California's earthquakes, fires and floods.

units.title: Violence Prevention and Personal Safety
units.big_idea: Recognizing danger, using refusal skills and telling trusted adults prevent violence.

units.title: Personal Health, Disease Prevention and Consumer Health
units.big_idea: Daily habits, immunity and smart consumer choices protect lifelong health.

units.title: Community Health and Advocacy
units.big_idea: Individuals can improve the health of their families, schools and communities.

weeks.topic: Dimensions of wellness and health skills
objectives: Describe physical, mental/emotional and social health

days.title: Wellness wheel
days.work: Rate yourself 1–5 on a wellness wheel (physical, emotional, social, intellectual, environmental) and shade it in.

days.title: Health skills
days.work: Match the eight CA health skills to middle-school scenarios and write one example for each.

days.title: Risk and protective factors
days.work: Sort 12 behaviors into risk or protective factors and explain two.

days.title: SMART goal
days.work: Write a SMART goal to strengthen the lowest section of your wellness wheel and make a tracker.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a quick check on wellness dimensions and share your goal with a parent.

weeks.topic: Decision making and valid health information

days.title: DECIDE model
days.work: Learn the DECIDE model (Define, Explore, Consider, Identify values, Decide, Evaluate) and apply it to a scenario about staying up late.

days.title: Source detective
days.work: Compare a .gov site, a health blog and an influencer video using a CRAAP-style checklist.

days.title: Bias and ads
days.work: Identify who profits from two health claims online and how that creates bias.

days.title: Practice decision
days.work: Use DECIDE on a scenario of a friend daring you to jump off a high wall.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Evaluate a new health website in writing and take a 6-question quiz.

objectives: Identify a wide range of emotions

days.title: Feelings wheel
days.work: Use a feelings wheel to identify 15 emotions beyond happy/sad/mad and give a situation for each.

days.title: Body cues
days.work: Map where you feel anger, anxiety and excitement in your body on an outline.

days.title: Triggers
days.work: Track emotional triggers in a journal for two days.

days.title: Healthy expression
days.work: Sort responses to anger into healthy and unhealthy and role-play two healthy responses.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a journal entry analyzing one emotion, its trigger and your response; complete a check.

days.title: Fight or flight
days.work: Learn the body's stress response and label hormone and body effects on a diagram.

days.title: Good vs. bad stress
days.work: Classify 10 situations as eustress or distress.

days.title: Stress inventory
days.work: Complete a middle-school stress inventory and identify your top three stressors.

days.title: Stress and health
days.work: Read about how long-term stress affects sleep, immunity and concentration.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a stress-concepts quiz.

days.title: Breathing
days.work: Practice box breathing and 4-7-8 breathing; record pulse before and after.

days.title: Muscle relaxation
days.work: Follow a progressive muscle relaxation script and journal how you feel.

days.title: Time management
days.work: Plan the coming week in a planner, blocking schoolwork, activity, chores and rest.

days.title: Coping toolbox
days.work: Build a coping toolbox of 8 strategies (exercise, music, talking, art, nature, etc.).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a personal stress-management plan and use one strategy daily for a week.

days.title: Strengths inventory
days.work: List 10 personal strengths and ask a family member to add three.

days.title: Self-talk
days.work: Rewrite 6 negative self-talk statements as realistic positive ones.

days.title: Growth mindset
days.work: Read a short article on brain growth with practice and write about something you improved with effort.

days.title: Resilience story
days.work: Read a biography excerpt of someone who overcame adversity and identify resilience traits.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Set a mental-health goal and complete a check on self-esteem concepts.

weeks.topic: Media and social media influences on emotions
objectives: Analyze social media's effect on mood and self-image

days.title: Comparison trap
days.work: Discuss how curated posts lead to comparison and list three edited-reality examples.

days.title: Screen-time log
days.work: Log screen use and mood for two days and look for patterns.

days.title: Algorithms
days.work: Learn how algorithms keep users scrolling and identify design features that do this.

days.title: Media plan
days.work: Write a family media plan with screen-free times and zones.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take the Emotions and Stress unit test.

days.title: Qualities
days.work: Rank 12 friendship qualities and explain your top three.

days.title: Healthy vs. unhealthy
days.work: Sort friendship behaviors (support, gossip, exclusion, honesty, control) into a spectrum chart.

days.title: Boundaries
days.work: Practice setting a boundary with a friend in 3 role-plays.

days.title: Making friends
days.work: Plan ways to make new friends through clubs, sports or co-ops.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a letter describing what kind of friend you want to be; complete a check.

objectives: Distinguish passive, aggressive and assertive communication

days.title: Three styles
days.work: Watch or act out passive, aggressive and assertive responses to the same situation and compare.

days.title: I-messages
days.work: Rewrite 6 blaming statements as I-messages (I feel... when... because... I need...).

days.title: Active listening
days.work: Practice paraphrasing in a 5-minute conversation with a family member.

days.title: Nonverbal
days.work: Practice assertive body language and tone in a mirror.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Perform an assertive communication role-play scored with a rubric.

days.title: Conflict causes
days.work: List common causes of conflict among middle schoolers and family members.

days.title: Resolution steps
days.work: Learn steps: cool down, take turns telling, listen, brainstorm solutions, agree, follow up.

days.title: Sibling scenario
days.work: Use the steps to resolve a realistic sibling or friend conflict in a role-play.

days.title: Mediation
days.work: Act as a mediator for a scripted peer conflict.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a solution for a new conflict scenario using every step.

days.title: Types of pressure
days.work: Identify direct, indirect and online peer pressure in scenarios.

days.title: Positive pressure
days.work: Write examples of positive peer pressure you have experienced or given.

days.title: Family roles
days.work: Interview a family member about responsibilities and how communication works at home.

days.title: Family meeting
days.work: Lead a short family meeting using I-messages to plan an activity.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take the Relationships unit test.

days.title: Identity map
days.work: Create an identity map (culture, interests, family, abilities) and compare with a family member's.

days.title: Stereotypes
days.work: Identify stereotypes in 5 media examples and explain their harm.

days.title: Inclusion
days.work: Read a story about exclusion and rewrite the ending to show inclusion.

days.title: Respect in action
days.work: List ways to include people with disabilities, new students or different family structures.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph on how respect supports mental health; complete a check.

days.title: Defining bullying
days.work: Distinguish bullying (repeated, power imbalance) from conflict in 8 scenarios.

days.title: Forms
days.work: Chart physical, verbal, social/relational and cyber bullying with examples and effects.

days.title: Bystander roles
days.work: Learn bystander, upstander and reporter roles and practice safe upstander responses.

days.title: Reporting
days.work: Write a script for reporting bullying to a trusted adult.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a bullying scenario quiz.

days.title: Digital footprint
days.work: Search a made-up name scenario and discuss what a digital footprint reveals and how long it lasts.

days.title: Privacy settings
days.work: Review privacy settings on a family device or app with a parent.

days.title: Scams and phishing
days.work: Identify red flags in 5 sample messages (phishing, prize scams, stranger requests).

days.title: Online strangers
days.work: Role-play refusing and reporting an online stranger asking for photos or to meet.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a Common Sense digital citizenship lesson and quiz.

days.title: Cyberbullying
days.work: Analyze how cyberbullying differs from in-person bullying (audience, permanence, anonymity).

days.title: Stop, block, tell
days.work: Practice responses: don't reply, screenshot, block, tell a trusted adult.

days.title: Kindness campaign
days.work: Design a kindness or anti-bullying poster or short video.

days.title: Present
days.work: Share the campaign with family or co-op.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take the Respect and Bullying Prevention unit test.

objectives: Recognize signs of depression and anxiety

days.title: Mental health continuum
days.work: Place examples on a mental health continuum (thriving to struggling).

days.title: Depression and anxiety
days.work: Read KidsHealth articles and list warning signs of each.

days.title: Stigma
days.work: Discuss myths about mental illness and rewrite them as facts.

days.title: Treatment works
days.work: Learn about counseling and treatment and why getting help early matters.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a signs-and-symptoms matching check.

days.title: Resources
days.work: List school, community and crisis resources including the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline.

days.title: Helping a friend
days.work: Learn the steps: notice, ask, listen, tell a trusted adult, and practice with a scenario.

days.title: When to tell
days.work: Discuss why some secrets must be shared with an adult to keep someone safe.

days.title: Self-care plan
days.work: Write a personal self-care plan for hard days.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Create a resource card and take the Mental Health unit quiz.

objectives: Plan prevention for falls, burns, poisonings

days.title: Injury facts
days.work: Read data on the leading causes of injury for kids 10–14 and graph the top five.

days.title: Home audit
days.work: Complete a home safety audit with a parent (smoke and CO alarms, cords, chemicals, stairs).

days.title: Kitchen safety
days.work: List rules for preventing burns and cuts and practice safe stove use with an adult.

days.title: Poison prevention
days.work: Check chemical storage and post the Poison Control number.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a home safety action plan and complete a check.

days.title: Water safety
days.work: Learn about drowning prevention, rip currents and life-jacket fit for pools, lakes and beaches.

days.title: Concussions
days.work: Read about concussion signs and why to stop playing and tell an adult.

days.title: Protective gear
days.work: Inspect sports gear and check helmet fit using the 2-V-1 rule.

days.title: Heat illness
days.work: Learn signs of heat exhaustion and heat stroke and prevention steps.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Create a sports safety checklist and take a quiz.

days.title: Road rules
days.work: Learn CA rules for cyclists and pedestrians, including helmet law under 18.

days.title: Bike check
days.work: Do an ABC quick check (air, brakes, chain) and ride a safe route with a parent.

days.title: Distractions
days.work: Discuss phone and headphone distraction while walking or riding.

days.title: Risk influences
days.work: Analyze stunt videos and peer dares that encourage risky behavior.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Map a safe route to a local destination and explain hazards.

objectives: Treat minor wounds, burns and nosebleeds

days.title: Check-Call-Care
days.work: Learn the Check-Call-Care steps and practice scene safety checks.

days.title: Bleeding
days.work: Practice direct pressure and bandaging on a family member with gloves.

days.title: Burns
days.work: Learn first aid for minor burns (cool water, cover) and when to get help.

days.title: Nosebleeds and sprains
days.work: Practice nosebleed care and RICE for sprains.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Inventory and restock the home first aid kit and complete a skills check.

objectives: Respond to choking and allergic reactions

days.title: Choking
days.work: Learn signs of choking and practice abdominal-thrust hand position on a pillow (no thrusts on people).

days.title: Allergic reactions
days.work: Learn signs of anaphylaxis and how an epinephrine auto-injector trainer is used.

days.title: Hands-only CPR intro
days.work: Watch an American Heart Association Hands-Only CPR video and practice compression rhythm on a pillow.

days.title: 911 or not?
days.work: Decide in 10 scenarios whether to call 911, call a parent, or give first aid.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take the Injury Prevention and First Aid unit test.

days.title: 911 calls
days.work: Learn what dispatchers ask and practice a mock 911 call with a parent playing dispatcher.

days.title: Know your info
days.work: Memorize your address and parents' numbers and set up an ICE contact.

days.title: Local resources
days.work: Locate nearest fire station, hospital and police station on a map.

days.title: Home alone safety
days.work: Write home-alone rules with a parent.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a mock-call rubric and contact card.

objectives: Practice drop, cover and hold on

days.title: Earthquake science
days.work: Review why California has earthquakes and what to do indoors, outdoors and in a car.

days.title: Drill
days.work: Practice Drop, Cover and Hold On in 3 rooms and identify safe spots.

days.title: Fire escape plan
days.work: Draw a home floor plan with two exits from each room and a meeting place.

days.title: Fire drill
days.work: Run a family fire drill and time it; practice stop, drop and roll and crawling low.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Answer a quiz on earthquake and fire safety.

days.title: Wildfire and smoke
days.work: Learn evacuation zones and how to read the Air Quality Index during wildfire smoke.

days.title: Go-bag
days.work: Pack or list a 72-hour go-bag using the Ready.gov checklist.

days.title: Family plan
days.work: Complete a family communication plan with an out-of-area contact.

days.title: Help others
days.work: Plan how to help a neighbor, pet or elderly relative in an emergency.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Present the family emergency plan and take the Preparedness unit quiz.

objectives: Describe dangers of weapons and gangs

days.title: Types of violence
days.work: Discuss physical, verbal and emotional violence and their effects.

days.title: Warning signs
days.work: List warning signs of potential violence and why to tell an adult.

days.title: Weapons
days.work: Learn the rule if you see a gun: don't touch, leave, tell an adult.

days.title: Gangs
days.work: Read about gang recruitment and list positive alternatives.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Role-play de-escalating a heated argument; complete a check.

days.title: Trust your gut
days.work: Discuss intuition and practice identifying uh-oh feelings in scenarios.

days.title: Boundaries
days.work: Learn personal-boundary rights and practice saying no to unwanted touch or requests.

days.title: Grooming warning signs
days.work: Learn warning signs such as secrets, gifts and isolation from adults or online contacts.

days.title: Escape plan
days.work: Practice No-Go-Tell and create a code word with your family.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take the Violence Prevention and Personal Safety unit quiz.

weeks.topic: Personal hygiene and dental care for adolescents

days.title: Hygiene review
days.work: Review skin, hair and body odor care and update your hygiene routine for middle school.

days.title: Acne myths
days.work: Sort acne myths and facts using KidsHealth and plan a gentle skin routine.

days.title: Dental health
days.work: Learn about gingivitis and practice proper flossing.

days.title: Sports hygiene
days.work: List hygiene rules for sports gear, showers and preventing athlete's foot.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a hygiene self-assessment and quiz.

days.title: Sleep needs
days.work: Learn why 9–12 hours matter for preteens and keep a 3-night sleep log.

days.title: Screens and sleep
days.work: Discuss blue light and phones in bedrooms and plan a device curfew.

days.title: Hearing
days.work: Use a sound meter app to measure common noises and learn safe headphone volume (60/60 rule).

days.title: Sun and eyes
days.work: Read a sunscreen label, check the UV index and learn the 20-20-20 eye rule.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a personal health practice goal and take a quiz.

weeks.topic: Communicable diseases and the immune system

days.title: Pathogens
days.work: Compare bacteria, viruses, fungi and protozoa and give a disease example for each.

days.title: How germs spread
days.work: Model germ spread with glitter on hands and objects around the house.

days.title: Handwashing test
days.work: Test glitter removal with water only vs. 20-second soap wash and record results.

days.title: Immune defenses
days.work: Draw the body's lines of defense (skin, mucus, white blood cells, antibodies) and explain how vaccines work.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a communicable disease quiz.

days.title: Chronic diseases
days.work: Research one chronic disease (asthma, diabetes, heart disease, cancer) and make a fact card.

days.title: Asthma
days.work: Learn asthma triggers and how an inhaler helps; discuss how to help a friend having an attack.

days.title: Risk factors
days.work: Sort controllable and uncontrollable risk factors for chronic disease.

days.title: Family history
days.work: Complete a simple family health history with a parent.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph on habits that lower chronic disease risk; complete a check.

days.title: Ad claims
days.work: Analyze 4 health-product ads for claims, techniques and missing information.

days.title: Comparison shopping
days.work: Compare name-brand and generic versions of a product by ingredients and unit price.

days.title: Quackery
days.work: Identify red flags of health fraud (miracle cure, secret formula, testimonials only).

days.title: Decide
days.work: Use DECIDE to choose a sunscreen or toothpaste and justify the choice.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Complete a consumer-health worksheet.

days.title: Providers
days.work: Match 10 health-care providers to what they do.

days.title: Check-up prep
days.work: Write questions to ask at your next check-up and learn what a well-child visit includes.

days.title: Pharmacist role
days.work: Read a prescription label and list questions to ask a pharmacist.

days.title: Community services
days.work: Locate a local clinic, dentist and public health department online.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Take the Personal and Consumer Health unit test.

days.title: Air quality
days.work: Check the local AQI for a week and graph it.

days.title: Water and noise
days.work: Learn about safe drinking water and noise pollution in your community.

days.title: Trash audit
days.work: Conduct a one-day household trash audit and plan reduce/reuse/recycle steps.

days.title: Public health
days.work: Research what your county public health department does.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Choose a community health issue for your advocacy project and justify it.

objectives: Plan and create an advocacy project

days.title: Research
days.work: Gather 4 facts from valid sources about your chosen issue (kindness, emergency preparedness, sun safety, clean air).

days.title: Plan
days.work: Identify audience, message and call to action.

days.title: Create
days.work: Produce a poster, brochure, slide show or short video.

days.title: Rehearse
days.work: Practice a 3-minute presentation and get feedback.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Revise using an advocacy rubric.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present your advocacy project to family, co-op or a community group.

days.title: Review game
days.work: Play a review game on mental health, safety and personal health.

days.title: Final assessment
days.work: Take the end-of-year health assessment.

days.title: Goal review
days.work: Review your wellness wheel from week 1 and re-rate each area.

days.title: Reflect
days.work: Write a reflection on your growth and a summer health and safety plan.
